messages:
Ava: Hey team — PR #20501 ready for merge but needs runtime/infra/sec eyes. Changes: fallback policy for eviction, adjust batch kernel selection heuristics, small orch config flag. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/20501
Diego: quick skim — platform changes look non-blocking. main risk is latency regressions with the new kernel heuristics. do runtime folks have perf numbers? :mag:
Lena: I'll take a look. do we have benchmark runs? also what's the canary plan?
Ava: thx! perf runs in the PR CI: `tests/perf/kernel_heuristics.py` + bench scripts. CI shows 95th/p99 tokens ~ +2ms on long-sequence tails. Canary: us-west 10% traffic for 2 hours, auto-rollback if error rate > 0.5%.
Sam: infra question — does this require infra-side config change or rolling nodes? if so we need a maintenance window.
Ava: no node restarts; purely runtime routing config and a flag we flip via the orch rollout. no infra tenant changes.
Maya: security quick Q: does this touch KMS/HSM or introduce new inbound endpoints? need to clear that before merge.
Ava: negative on KMS/HSM. no new external endpoints. only internal routing + kernel pick logic. I also scanned for secrets.
jenkins-bot: CI / unit tests: all checks passed ✅
Lena: ok pulled the branch and ran local perf with the bench harness — numbers align with CI. found one minor comment nit in `kernel_selector.py` but not blocking. approving now :white_check_mark:
Maya: security +1. please add a short note in the PR describing threat-model checks you ran (no KMS, no new endpoints, data plane unchanged).
Sam: infra +1 — no infra ops required, no rolling restarts.
Diego: platform +1 for merge window. recommend merging during 14:00–17:00 PT so we can watch metrics.
Ava: thanks all — planning to merge in 30m into `main`. tagging runtime/infra/sec for post-merge watch. will post canary dashboard link when live :rocket:
